paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Kingship, Holiness, and Justice

easy.q: Who is described as reigning at the beginning of the psalm?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “let the people tremble” and “let the earth be moved.”
easy.q: What happens to the people and the earth because of the LORD’s presence?

easy.explanation: The verse declares, “for it is holy,” referring to His great and terrible name.
easy.q: What quality is attributed to the LORD in verse 3?

medium.explanation: Verse 4 says, “The king’s strength also loveth judgment.”
medium.q: What is the king’s strength said to love in verse 4?

medium.explanation: The verse says He establishes equity and executes judgment and righteousness in Jacob.
medium.q: According to verse 4, what does the LORD establish and execute?

answers: His holiness causes them to ignore Him
His holiness is connected with awe, praise, and trembling
His holiness prevents Him from being king
medium.explanation: The people tremble and praise His great and terrible name because He is holy.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s holiness and the people’s response in verses 1–3?

answers: The LORD reigns, His holiness is recognized, and His justice is described
Moses prays, the Temple is built, and a battle begins
The nations crown a king, offer sacrifices, and leave the land
challenge.explanation: These verses present the LORD as king, emphasize His holiness, and describe His righteous rule.

answers: Judgment has no place in His kingdom
The LORD loves just rule and carries it out righteously
Judgment belongs only to earthly rulers
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the king’s love of judgment with establishing equity and executing righteousness.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between the king’s love of judgment and His execution of righteousness?

answers: He is exalted and inspires awe
He depends on the nations for help
challenge.explanation: He sits between the cherubims, is high above the people, and has a great and terrible name.
challenge.q: Which characteristic is shared by the LORD’s descriptions in verses 1–4?

paragraphs.title: Worship and the Lord’s Response to His Servants

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Exalt ye the LORD our God, and worship at his footstool.”
easy.q: What are the people called to do in verse 5?

easy.explanation: Verse 6 names Moses, Aaron, and Samuel.
easy.q: Who are named among those who called upon the LORD’s name?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “they called upon the LORD, and he answered them.”
easy.q: What did the LORD do when His servants called upon Him?

answers: He spoke to them, and they kept His testimonies
medium.explanation: The LORD spoke to them in the cloudy pillar, and they kept His testimonies and ordinance.
medium.q: What does verse 7 describe about the relationship between the LORD and Moses, Aaron, and Samuel?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “He spake unto them in the cloudy pillar.”
medium.q: Where did the LORD speak to them according to verse 7?

answers: He answered and forgave them, yet took vengeance on their inventions
medium.explanation: The verse says that He answered them, forgave them, and took vengeance on their inventions.
medium.q: How does verse 8 describe the LORD’s treatment of His servants?

answers: The servants called upon the LORD, kept His ordinance, and received His answer
Keeping the testimonies prevented them from praying
The LORD answered only those who rejected His ordinance
challenge.explanation: The passage presents servants who call upon the LORD, keep His testimonies, and receive His response.
challenge.q: What connection is made between keeping the testimonies and receiving an answer from the LORD in verses 6–8?

challenge.explanation: The LORD is described as forgiving them while also taking vengeance on their inventions.
challenge.q: What two seemingly different actions are attributed to the LORD in verse 8?

answers: They are presented as servants who called upon the LORD and kept His ordinances
They are presented as kings of foreign nations
They refused to hear the LORD’s voice
challenge.explanation: They are named among those who called upon the LORD, and the following verses describe His communication with His servants.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the inclusion of Moses, Aaron, and Samuel together?

paragraphs.title: The Holy Mountain and the Lord’s Holiness

easy.explanation: The verse says, “worship at his holy hill.”
easy.q: Where are the people called to worship in verse 9?

answers: Because the LORD our God is holy
easy.explanation: The verse concludes, “for the LORD our God is holy.”
easy.q: Why are the people called to exalt and worship the LORD?

answers: A call to honor and worship the LORD at His holy hill
A description of war between nations
easy.explanation: The verse calls the people to exalt the LORD and worship at His holy hill.
easy.q: What does the final verse contain?

answers: The holiness of the hill is connected with the holiness of the LORD
The hill is described as having no holiness
medium.explanation: The people worship at His holy hill because “the LORD our God is holy.”
medium.q: What connection does verse 9 make between the holy hill and the LORD?

answers: It is associated with the LORD and set apart for Him
It is a place of fear without worship
medium.explanation: The possessive “his” connects the holy hill with the LORD, and the verse calls for worship there.
medium.q: What does the phrase “his holy hill” show about the hill?

answers: The call to exalt and worship is supported by the reason that the LORD is holy
The ending cancels the command at the beginning
The two parts have no connection
medium.explanation: The word “for” introduces the reason for worship: “the LORD our God is holy.”
medium.q: What is the relationship between the beginning and the end of verse 9?

answers: It joins the exaltation of the LORD, worship, and His holiness
It changes from holiness to a description of war
It describes only the actions of Moses and Aaron
challenge.explanation: The verse calls for exaltation and worship and ends by emphasizing the LORD’s holiness.
challenge.q: How does verse 9 summarize central ideas of the psalm?

answers: Honor for the LORD is also connected with the place set apart for Him
There is no longer any need to honor the LORD
The holy hill is more important than the LORD
challenge.explanation: Both verses call for worship, and the final verse connects worship with the LORD’s holy hill.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the movement from worship at the LORD’s footstool in verse 5 to worship at His holy hill in verse 9?

challenge.explanation: The word “for” introduces the reason: “the LORD our God is holy.”
challenge.q: Which word in verse 9 introduces the reason why the LORD should be exalted and worshipped?
